form_analysis.feedback: Excellent and highly focused aftercare form for age spot (solar lentigo) removal, primarily via laser/IPL/cryotherapy. Provides crystal-clear, phased guidance specific to the spot-by-spot treatment process. Outstanding emphasis on sun protection as the definitive preventive measure. Expertly covers the crusting/flaking timeline, PIH prevention, and realistic expectations for clearance. Strong safety protocols and series treatment emphasis.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is specifically designed for the removal of individual age spots (solar lentigines) via laser, intense pulsed light (IPL), or cryotherapy. Proper care of each treated spot is essential for it to heal cleanly, prevent darkening, and ensure it does not return. Meticulous sun protection is the cornerstone of success.

instructions.general_directive: Follow this guidance meticulously for each treated spot. Healing occurs over 10-21 days per spot. Your commitment to sun protection will determine long-term results.

sections.title: Pre-Treatment Preparation
sections.content: You MUST have avoided sun exposure and tanning on the treatment area for 4 WEEKS prior. No active tan or sunburn. Disclose any history of keloid scarring or abnormal wound healing.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Response (Per Spot)
sections.content: Each treated spot will instantly darken, turning GREY, BROWN, or BLACK. This is the desired effect—the pigment has been targeted. The spot may swell slightly and feel sensitive. The surrounding skin may be red. This reaction is confined to the spot itself.

sections.title: Phase 1: Crust Formation (Days 1-7)
items: The darkened spot will form a thin, dark, well-defined crust (scab). This crust is delicate and protects the healing skin beneath.
DO NOT PICK, SCRATCH, OR WET THIS CRUST. Picking will cause scarring and increase the risk of the spot returning darker (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation).
Cleanse your face gently, avoiding direct scrubbing on the spots.
Apply the provided healing ointment (e.g., petroleum jelly) to each crust 1-2 times daily to keep it moist and protected. Do not let it dry out.

sections.title: Phase 2: Flaking & Separation (Days 7-14)
sections.content: The crust will begin to lift at the edges and eventually flake off, often looking like a small, dark "flake" or "seed." It may come off in the shower or with gentle cleansing. LET IT FALL OFF NATURALLY. Do not aid the process. Underneath, the skin will be pink or pale.

sections.title: Phase 3: Pink & Blending (Days 14-60+)
sections.content: The healed area will be pink or slightly lighter than your surrounding skin. This is new skin without pigment. It will gradually blend in over 4-8 weeks. During this time, it is VULNERABLE to sun and must be protected to prevent it from tanning and becoming a new dark spot.

sections.title: Sun Protection (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
sections.content: Sun exposure caused your age spots; it will bring them back. For 4 WEEKS BEFORE and 3-6 MONTHS AFTER treatment (and lifelong): Apply a broad-spectrum SPF 30-50+ to the entire area every single day, even if cloudy. The healed pink spots need extra protection—consider a zinc oxide stick directly on them. Wear a hat and protective clothing. This is the most important part of your aftercare.

sections.title: Activity & Environmental Restrictions
items: Avoid strenuous sweating and exercise for 48-72 hours to prevent irritation and infection of the crusts.
Avoid swimming in chlorinated pools, hot tubs, or the ocean for 7 days.
Avoid saunas and steam rooms for 5-7 days.

sections.title: Skincare Product Restrictions (On the Spots)
items: Until crusts fall off: Do not apply any active serums, retinoids, acids, or exfoliants directly on the spots.

After healing (2+ weeks): You may resume your regular skincare, but continue to protect the spots with sunscreen. Your practitioner may recommend a lightening agent (like hydroquinone) for the surrounding area to prevent new spots, but not on the newly healed pink skin until fully blended.

sections.title: Makeup Application
sections.content: Do not apply makeup directly over crusting spots. Once the crusts have fallen off and the skin is smooth (after 7-10 days), you may gently apply makeup to camouflage any pinkness. Use clean tools.

sections.title: Preventing Post-Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation (PIH)
sections.content: The main risk is the spot healing darker than before. Prevent this by: 1) Not picking the crust. 2) Religious sun protection. 3) Avoiding irritation to the spot. If the pink area starts to turn brown, contact your practitioner; they may prescribe a lightening cream.

sections.title: Infection & Scarring Awareness
sections.content: Signs of infection in a spot: increasing pain, redness spreading from the spot, pus, or swelling. Contact your practitioner. Hypertrophic or keloid scarring is rare but possible, especially on the chest and shoulders. Report any raised, itchy, or growing scar tissue.

sections.title: Results Timeline & Treatment Series
items: A spot is considered successfully treated when the crust falls off to reveal pink skin that later blends in.
Some spots may require a second treatment if pigment remains after the first session (not all pigment cells are destroyed).
For multiple spots, a series of 1-3 treatments spaced 4-8 weeks apart may be needed to clear all areas.
A follow-up is typically scheduled at 6-8 weeks to assess healing and determine if further treatment is needed.
Complete clearance is the goal, but 80-95% improvement is typical and excellent.

sections.title: Long-Term Prevention
sections.content: New age spots will form with sun exposure. Maintain daily sunscreen use on all exposed skin (face, hands, chest, arms). Consider using topical antioxidants (Vitamin C) and retinoids to protect skin cells. Annual maintenance treatments may be needed for new spots.

patient_declaration.reading_confirmation: Removing age spots is a straightforward process, but its success depends entirely on your aftercare, especially sun protection. Please read and commit fully.
patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Your practitioner can show you the best way to apply sunscreen to healed spots. Ask if you are unsure about the healing stage of any spot.
patient_declaration.declaration_text: I confirm that I have read and understood the aftercare instructions for my age spot removal treatment. I understand that each spot will darken, crust, and flake, and I will not pick at them. I accept that strict, lifelong sun protection is mandatory to prevent recurrence and will apply sunscreen daily. I will contact the clinic with any concerns about infection or darkening of a treated spot.

clarity_notes: Perfectly tailored to the very specific and common concern of discrete age spot removal.
recommendations: Could include a note about the difference in healing between flat spots and slightly raised seborrheic keratoses (if treated), as the latter may have a more pronounced crust.
Add a tip for treating spots on the hands: wear gloves for washing dishes/gardening and apply sunscreen even when driving.
Consider mentioning that cryotherapy spots may form a blister instead of a dark crust; advise not to pop it and to follow similar protective care.
